newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Mar 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Mar 18.

text.p: Violent offending and traffic offences -- two areas targeted by police -- dropped last year but all other crime increased. Police Commissioner Peter Doone, who issued the 1996 crime statistics, has said the road toll was the lowest for 32 years and violent offending was down 0.9 percent, the first decrease in seven years. But overall, reported crime increased two percent, with the number of incidents climbing from 506,359 to 516,360. Page 1.

Ten of the 25 women who have served on the frigate Wellington when alleged sexual harassment took place and left the navy or said they wanted to leave, defence officials said on Monday. Only 39 of the 225 male crew- 17 percent against the 40 percent rate for women -- have given similar notice. Labour MP Geoff Braybrooke said on Monday that the Defence Force had suspended work on reviewing Human Rights Act compliance because of lack of funding. Page 2.

ACT NZ MP Rodney Hide is cranking up his campaign to cut former MPs travel perks, with questions to Speaker Doug Kidd and a plan to poll the views of each MP. About $1 million is spent each year to subsidise air travel for former MPs and their spouses. Ministers are eligible after two terms in Parliament, MPs after three terms. Page 2.

ACT NZ MPs are to consider introducing a private member's bill to Parliament to hold a public referendum on the future of the five Maori seats. Party leader Richard Prebble was undeterred on Monday by criticism after his call at the weekend
for a review of the seats, all held by NZ First. Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters branded Prebble's call as "cheap-shot racism". Page 2.

Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters's alleged assault on National MP John Banks will come under the scrutiny of Parliament's privileges committee on Wednesday. Procedures for the hearing are the subject of behind-the-scenes political wrangling, sources say. The committee is expected to meet on Wednesday evening to start investigating the late-night fracas between Peters and Banks outside the debating chambers two weeks ago. Page 2.

Retail sales figures for January issued on Monday should keep monetary conditions tighter than the Reserve Bank would like, Bankers Trust chief economist David Plank said. Retail sales rose 3.4 percent in January compared with sales in December after adjustment for seasonal effects and price inflation, Statistics NZ said on Monday. Plank said he had expected an increase of two percent. Page 8.

Households in the Wellington region should be able to chose a different power company in two to three years with the introduction of sophisticated metering, according to TransAlta chief executive Mike Underhill. Speaking to a power industry conference in Wellington on Monday, Underhill said he believed there would be a competitive market for small domestic customers in two or three years. Page 8.

The national median price for houses sold in February was $160,000, Real Estate Institute President Colin Brown said. "We have not previously seen the national median at this level," Brown said. "The residential real estate market is continuing to be very active and home buyers appear to be making the most of competitive interest rates currently available." Page 8.

A High Court decision to give half the future output of the Kapuni gas field to the Shell-Todd consortium appeared to be at odds with natural justice, Natural Gas Corporation chairman Mike Smith said on Monday. His company had been pleased that the
Court in February had upheld the original 1967 contract between the field's operators -- Shell-Todd -- and its subsequent owners, Smith told an energy conference in Wellington. Page 8.

Listed office chair maker Damba Holdings has reported a 78 percent fall in its full-year after-tax profit to $143,000. The result, contrasting with the $672,000 profit reported for the year ended December 31, 1995, was achieved on a one percent revenue rise to $13.89 million. New Zealand sales were down 2.5 percent at $11.8 million, with pre-tax operating profit down 35 percent at $868,000. Page 8.

A shortage of senior executives in finance and marketing has pushed up salary packages on both sides of the Tasman and produced a "head-hunter's paradise" in these fields, a review of executive salaries has found. David Bassett, general manager of management consultants Cullen Egan Dell, said high salary packages offered by Asian companies were attracting top Australian executives, forcing Australian companies to recruit across the Tasman. Page 8.
